issues.description: The problem statement and template specify an addGuestStudents method with two parameters (int, String) including a reason, but the solution implements addGuestStudents with only a single int parameter. This mismatch in method signature creates confusion about the expected API and would prevent code relying on the two-parameter signature from compiling against the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specified signature. Change the solution's method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update its body to add the new guest students (e.g., numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents) and optionally handle or log the provided reason. Alternatively, if the intended design is a single-parameter method, update the problem statement and template to specify addGuestStudents(int) so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an integer number of new guest students plus a reason String), but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only an int parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (missing String parameter) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the required API described in the exercise and the provided solution, creating confusion for students about the expected method signature and its usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the exercise API: change the solution method signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and handle or document the reason parameter (e.g., store it, log it, or ignore it with a comment). Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unnecessary, update the problem statement/UML to remove the String parameter so the specification matches the implementation.
